segments.t: Meanwhile, Chef Barinov tries to apologize to the television crew after Nagiyev chased them out of the kitchen, but when they consider filming rival chef Elena Pavlovna instead, Viktor refuses to give up his spotlight. Let's listen in Russian.
Вы уж извините, что так вышло.
Виктор Петрович, мы не можем долго ждать.
Я же сказал, договорюсь с Нагиевым.

'I will talk to Nagiyev.' Chef Viktor uses the first-person pronoun in the case required by the Russian verb or preposition.
'In a day or two he will cool down.' Chef Viktor keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.

'Viktor Petrovich, we cannot wait that long.' Elena places the negative particle directly before the verb or predicate to negate the statement.
'Our deadlines are burning.' Elena uses natural conversational word order here to highlight the most important part of the reply.
'We will find someone else.' Elena keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.

'There is no need to ask anyone else.' Notice how Chef Viktor pairs a modal word or finite verb with an infinitive to express the action.

'I told you, I will make a deal with Nagiyev.' Chef Viktor keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect.
'Well, all right then.' Elena keeps the sentence short and direct, relying on Russian case endings to show how the words connect. Now let's replay the whole dialogue at natural speed.
